title: Is a paid job seva?
hook: doing your job well is a way of serving
carry: seva is service with no reward in mind
tomorrow: a kid at the stall asks: why the plain steel bracelet?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a scale turned back to zero and a count that stalled on tera: fair weights. Then Simran posted about her shift, and the comments started.

A photo of an apron and a crate of peaches, captioned: today's seva, six hours at the stall. The first comment is a heart from Maya. The second is from Jasleen: um, it's not seva if they pay you. Simran types a reply. Deletes it. Types it again. Jasleen isn't being mean. She just takes the word seriously. And so does Simran.
screen: `TODAY'S SEVA: MY SHIFT.` → `JASLEEN: NOT IF THEY PAY YOU.` → `TYPE, DELETE, TYPE.`

segments.voice: Let both views speak. Jasleen's first. Seva is selfless service, given freely: at the gurdwara, in the langar, for anyone in need. In the Sukhmani Sahib, on ang 286, Guru Arjan says, in paraphrase: the one who serves without wanting a reward reaches the Lord. Call a paid shift seva, and the word loses its edge. Her best case: keep seva clear of wages, so you can always tell the two apart. Now Simran's. Kirat, honest work, is itself part of the Sikh life, and the way you bring yourself to it, care, honesty, no shortcuts, can be the same way you bring yourself to the langar. Her best case: if service only happens on Sundays, the other six days are spent on something less. Look closely and they agree on more than the comments suggest. Neither thinks a paycheck makes work holy. Neither thinks a cashier can't serve the person in front of her. The real line is the one in Guru Arjan's verse: without wanting a reward. A wage is fine. Working only for the wage is the thing both are wary of. So Simran edits the caption: six hours at the stall, did the job as well as i could. And she keeps the word seva for her Sunday langar shift, where nobody pays anyone.
screen: `JASLEEN: SEVA IS GIVEN FREELY.` · `ANG 286: WITHOUT WANTING A REWARD.` · `SIMRAN: A JOB DONE WITH CARE SERVES.` · `WHERE THEY AGREE.` · then, large: `WORK AS SEVA.`

segments.voice: Choose one small task within reach, folding a towel, wiping a surface, straightening a shelf, and do it as well as you possibly can, slowly, corners and all. Then sit with the finished thing in view.
Work as seva. Doing your job well as a way of serving, without making the reward the reason.
Your line: seva is service with no reward in mind. The wage is fine; it just isn't the reason. Done for today.
